sense: how someone responds to what happens

terms.gloss: take (something) well or badly; react to
terms.grammar: irregular verb, with an adverb or animō + adjective; the thing as object, an accusative and infinitive, or dē + ablative
evidence: Cic. Phil. 10.15: quōmodo ferant veterānī exercitum Brūtum habēre (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 5.2.3: quōmodo Caesar ferret dē auctōritāte perscrīptā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin asks how a person bore a thing: aequō animō ferre, to take it calmly; graviter, molestē, aegrē ferre, to take it badly (Lewis & Short). Ferre is first of all to carry.

terms.gloss: a stirring of the mind, an emotional reaction
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.136: mōtūs animī nimiī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Any movement; of the mind, an impulse or emotion (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: quōmodo ferant veterānī exercitum Brūtum habēre
phrases.english: how the veterans would react to Brutus having an army

phrases.latin: hoc ēreptum esse, graviter et acerbē ferre
phrases.english: to take it hard and bitterly that this was snatched away

sources: Lewis & Short: fero · Lewis & Short: motus
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
